title: Uniform lower bounds for Collatz predecessor densities: paper and Lean proofs
description:
Lucas Valbuena, Collatz basin densities and canonical traces from first-passage stabilization. The paper proves a uniform inverse-linear lower bound for the natural density of every positive shortcut basin whose target is prime to three. The ordinary-map predecessor natural density satisfies the same bound. Weighted first-hit densities and canonical traces have corresponding uniform lower bounds.

The proof uses Mazur's weighted predecessor construction, Said Duran's coalescence theorem, and periodic source averaging. The inverse-linear form was proposed by Wirsching. The density and canonical-limit foundations use Tao's first-passage theorem and Mazur's natural-counting transport. All inputs are credited separately. No claim of an exhaustive novelty search is made. Divergence and additional cycles remain unresolved; the paper does not prove the Collatz conjecture.

The archive contains the paper, LaTeX source, theorem map, native Lean foundation, and additive proof bundle. Verification records distinguish fresh compilation and individual kernel checks from authenticated reuse of pinned dependencies. Audited results use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The current collection omits the earlier standalone matrix-obstruction and independent-second-proof papers; those remain in earlier repository releases.

Original code and documentation use MIT. Imported and adapted formal sources retain their Apache-2.0 or other original licenses and notices. The paper and LaTeX source use CC BY 4.0. Automated proof development and review are disclosed and do not constitute external peer review.
